answer: For marble surveys, knoll maps and sonnet editing, a market can grant one quota per certified secure chip. Validators check the manufacturer's certificate and a chip signature binding the epoch beacon to an account key. They record the chip serial and reject any second quota claimed with it, even under another key. Each extra identity needs another chip and its purchase cost; parallel accounts cannot reuse a recorded serial. This assumes the issuer certifies one nonexportable signing key per physical chip and validators share a correct registry.
